races.name: Proper Job Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Norman Fletcher
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter who will enjoy an uncontested lead on Good ground, but his recent form string of 9837-7 is modest and his jockey Miss Amber Jackson-Fennell will need to judge the fractions carefully; the STYLE_FIT flag is not an issue here as he is fulfilling his natural lead role, and his 2m1f Good ground record (sim-going 8/15, 1W3P) is adequate if not exceptional at this level.

runners_data.name: Roadshow
runners_data.note: A 247-day absence is the headline concern for Paul Nicholls' four-year-old, whose only win came over 17f Good last time he was fully fit; if fit enough to race prominently and track the leader, his Good-ground profile (sim-going 9/13) is a solid match, and the tongue-strap is retained, but the layoff makes him vulnerable to being short of peak condition at a critical stage.

runners_data.name: Saint Polo
runners_data.note: Won seven days ago and arrives fit and in form, with his 2m1f trip and Good ground perfectly matching his best efforts (sim-going 6/9, 1W3P); a genuine hold-up horse who will be ridden to come late, he needs enough pace in front to close into, which depends entirely on Norman Fletcher's tempo sustaining pressure.

runners_data.name: Chillhi
runners_data.note: Ran only ten days ago for Barry Murphy and showed a little more at 3m on Good last time, so stepping back to 2m1f on similar going is a slight question; a genuine closer (hg:tp) who will be ridden patiently by Mr Louis Burke, he needs the pace to be honest and will be finishing into any gaps that open in the straight.

runners_data.name: Cogital
runners_data.note: Veteran of 11 who won over 17f Good most recently, giving him live claims on Going — but as a genuine hold-up horse redistributed to the midfield map position, he faces the challenge that a slow early pace will not create the gaps he needs; his STYLE_FIT flag reflects the congestion of closers in this field, and at 11 his consistency is reliable without being explosive.

runners_data.name: Ugo Bingo
runners_data.note: Joseph Tizzard's seven-year-old has a prominent profile and has gone well at this trip on Good (sim-going 8/15), though his recent form of 4647-7 is uninspiring and Miss Heidi Palin will need to produce a career-best ride; his value is as a close tracker of the leader, and he is potentially better placed than his form suggests if the race is run to suit front-end types.

runners_data.name: Applejack Poet
runners_data.note: A 264-day absence is a significant flag for this eight-year-old who has been placed on Good going, and as a true hold-up horse shown in midfield due to the redistribution, the long layoff makes it doubly hard to expect him to finish from off the pace in peak condition; his Good ground profile (sim-going 14/15) is extensive but the form string includes falls and pulled-ups, and Miss Imogen Mathias will have her hands full.

runners_data.name: Linden Lane
runners_data.note: Consistent placer (0W4P in last five, three thirds) who brings freshness at 11 days since last run and races for a small yard; her natural style is hold-up but she has been mapped to midfield given the rear-end congestion in this field — her real strength is finishing into a place, and Eleanor Williams will need luck in running if the pace doesn't fire enough to bring her into the picture.

races.paceDynamic: Norman Fletcher is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate a sustainable, uncontested gallop from the outset on Good ground at Newton Abbot. Roadshow and Ugo Bingo are the likeliest to press from prominent positions, but neither is a true pace-forcing type, so the tempo is unlikely to be severe enough to set up a dramatic finish for closers. Saint Polo, Chillhi, Cogital, Applejack Poet, and Linden Lane all carry genuine hold-up profiles, but the field holds more hold-up and back-of-the-field types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Cogital, Applejack Poet, and Linden Lane are the truest hold-up horses and are least likely to secure their natural position given the congestion behind the pace. With a controlled, lone-leader tempo on a flat, fair surface, this race shape strongly favours front-runners and close-tracking prominent types who can enjoy cover and pounce in the straight without needing a truly searching pace to bring them into contention.

watchPoints.text: Norman Fletcher's jumping must be tracked from flag to flag — any error at a hurdle under the amateur rider Miss Amber Jackson-Fennell could immediately hand the initiative to Roadshow or Ugo Bingo, transforming the race shape.

Roadshow's 247-day absence is the single biggest unknown in the field; if P F Nicholls has him fully wound up he could press the front-runner and lift the tempo, but if he blows up mid-race the entire pace picture collapses into a processional finish.

The cluster of hold-up horses (Saint Polo, Chillhi, Cogital, Applejack Poet, Linden Lane) competing for the same ground late in the race creates significant traffic risk — watch for any of them getting squeezed for room on the home turn if the pace is modest.

Applejack Poet's 264-day layoff combined with a STYLE_FIT redistribution flag makes him a horse to monitor early — if he shows signs of greenness or poor jumping after such a long absence, he could become an obstacle for horses travelling behind him.

races.name: Celebrate Racing Staff Week Juvenile Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
Happy Birthday June O'Dwyer Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Coumeenoole
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's in-form seven-year-old (11 wins from 26 starts for the yard over 14 days) returns just 19 days after a win over an equivalent trip on good ground, racing in his favoured front-running role; the STYLE_FIT flag is minor here as he is genuinely the controlling force, though any jumping error on this longer trip at Newton Abbot is the main risk.

runners_data.name: Outmaster
runners_data.note: Paul Nicholls' five-year-old arrives unbeaten in one hurdle start on good ground, and Freddie Gingell has a clear riding brief; 48 days off is not a concern for a Nicholls novice, and the proximity in OR to Coumeenoole (120 v 121) tells you this is a genuine two-horse race on paper.

runners_data.name: Bacardi Blue
runners_data.note: David Summersby's five-year-old holds up and lacks any win from recent hurdle starts, with form figures of 55-26 telling a consistent but modest story; the step up to 2m5½f could help on paper, but good going has not unlocked improvement and Bryan Carver's trainer is without a strike rate over 14 days.

runners_data.name: Ballinoulart
runners_data.note: Long-absent (596 days) and rated just OR 69, this eight-year-old has a natural instinct to race prominently — but the front positions in this field are firmly owned by Coumeenoole and Outmaster, so his true running style is effectively buried; amateur jockey Mr Richard Upton and a blank 14-day trainer record add further complication.

runners_data.name: Glenary
runners_data.note: Paul Gundry's five-year-old is lightly raced and returning from 396 days off, so fitness is a legitimate question mark despite the P/PU-2 form string suggesting latent ability; this hold-up type needs the race to fall apart up front, and the unknown element of a long absence makes its profile speculative rather than dangerous.

runners_data.name: Keep Off The Sugar
runners_data.note: J D Frost's five-year-old has shown only modest form (finishing 7th, then pulled up) with a form string of /00-7P and a going record of 3 places from 5 on good, so there is little to encourage confidence; a hold-up style in a race likely run at a fair but not extreme pace over 2m5½f does not create the late opportunity this runner needs.

races.paceDynamic: Coumeenoole is the confirmed pace-setter here and, with only Outmaster as a genuine challenger for the prominent positions, he is likely to control this race from the front at a sustainable, uncontested gallop over 2m5½f on good ground. Outmaster will sit close behind or alongside, but with no horse willing or able to truly pressure Coumeenoole, the pace is unlikely to be extreme — this sets up as a measured, front-runner-controlled affair rather than a gruelling test. The field holds more prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: Ballinoulart is a natural front-runner remapped to midfield because Coumeenoole and Outmaster will dominate those positions, making it very hard for Ballinoulart to fulfil its true role. A steady-to-fair pace over this trip on good ground at Newton Abbot strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and strike from the front two or three, rewarding Coumeenoole's natural position and the class of Outmaster to mount a late challenge — hold-up horses will need everything to fall perfectly from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Coumeenoole Controls And Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Coumeenoole dictates an uncontested lead and the pace remains measured throughout, allowing him to conserve energy for the run-in.
scenarios.body: If Coumeenoole dictates an uncontested lead and the pace remains measured throughout, allowing him to conserve energy for the run-in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Outmaster Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Outmaster settles beautifully off Coumeenoole's steady pace and uses superior class and freshness to wear him down in the final two hurdles.
scenarios.body: If Outmaster settles beautifully off Coumeenoole's steady pace and uses superior class and freshness to wear him down in the final two hurdles.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Capitalise On Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Coumeenoole's jumping falters or the pace proves deceptively taxing and the front two tire on the long run-in.
scenarios.body: If Coumeenoole's jumping falters or the pace proves deceptively taxing and the front two tire on the long run-in.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Ballinoulart Secures Position
scenarios.trigger: If the race somehow unfolds with early chaos or hesitation and Ballinoulart manages to reclaim a genuine prominent pitch.
scenarios.body: If the race somehow unfolds with early chaos or hesitation and Ballinoulart manages to reclaim a genuine prominent pitch.

watchPoints.text: Watch Coumeenoole's jumping — if Harry Skelton has him ping the early hurdles cleanly, the race is effectively his to control, but a mistake at any hurdle over this longer Newton Abbot trip could unwind the entire front-running plan.

Monitor Outmaster's position in the early stages — if Freddie Gingell elects to sit very close to Coumeenoole rather than a length or two off, the pace could quicken earlier than expected and turn the race into a two-horse duel that leaves the hold-up horses stranded.

Ballinoulart's ability to actually secure a prominent pitch will tell you quickly whether the race shape is orthodox — if he does get forward, the pace pressure on Coumeenoole increases marginally and Glenary's late run becomes marginally more viable.

Glenary's market move at the off is worth tracking given the lengthy absence of 396 days — if Gundry's stable has the horse cherry-ripe, the single previous run on good ground (placed) suggests raw ability that could surprise at big odds if the front two tire.

races.name: EBCS Hideout Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Marhaba The Champ
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator who needs a strong pace to deliver his finishing effort; recent form shows a drop to fifth last time from a prominent position, and the controlled tempo Phantom Gold is likely to set may not suit; 20 days since last run, hood fitted, Good ground poses no concern.|

runners_data.name: Phantom Gold
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner, rated 95 and recording a win on Good ground over similar trips; trainer has had three winners from 24 in the past fortnight suggesting decent yard form; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) is minor here since leading is arguably her natural role — but she does run occasionally from off the pace, so watch for early tactical calls from I J Power.|

runners_data.name: Katana
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer with four places from 13 starts on similar ground and a career best second last time; C Gethings rides from 12 days since last run, which is tight; needs the pace to strengthen to deliver, and the likely moderate tempo is her biggest obstacle.|

runners_data.name: Privilege
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 334 days off (311 days since a fall), which is the dominant concern here regardless of any tactical note; placed twice on Good at 18f, so trip and ground are fine, but that long layoff and hurdles fall cloud everything.|

runners_data.name: Chartwell Jock
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who has placed three times from 13 runs on similar ground; Sam Bowen takes the ride for Nick Scholfield, who has had one winner from nine in 14 days; hg:p (cheekpieces) applied and he ran an encouraging fourth last time — tracking the leader is his natural comfort zone.|

runners_data.name: Crab Road
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse who fades in the finish, which is a significant concern over 2m2½f on a track with a testing run-in; form string of 00PF-P tells a bleak story and his Good-going record (3 from 7) offers little comfort; only 11 days since last run.|

runners_data.name: Makinbecon
runners_data.note: Won over 18f on Good ground and holds a genuine hold-up profile, but the field's congestion at the rear means he is realistically racing further forward than ideal; the STYLE_FIT discount (0.92) reflects that compromise, and his trainer has had no winners from five in 14 days.|

runners_data.name: Warfleet
runners_data.note: Authentic hold-up type whose best effort — a recent third on Good over 17f — came from the back; the redistribution to midfield compresses his ability to deliver a late surge, and a STYLE_FIT of 0.90 confirms the shape may work against him despite competitive recent form.|

runners_data.name: Man Oh Man
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse placed twice from 14 runs on Good ground, but the redistribution forces him into midfield where his slow-build style loses its natural advantage; 26 days since last run, cheekpieces on, and his trainer has had nothing from three in the fortnight.|

runners_data.name: Bowling Shane
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type with a third last time over 16f on Good; tongue-tie applied and 19 days since last run; sits most comfortably when dropped in late but will need a stronger gallop than Phantom Gold is likely to set; C Boultbee-Brooks has had no winners from one recent runner.|

runners_data.name: Saucats
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with three places from 15 starts on similar ground and a second last time; tongue-tie and hood in use; however, the redistribution to midfield and a STYLE_FIT of 0.90 mean he is unlikely to get the clear late passage that suits him, and trainer has had no winners from ten in 14 days.|

runners_data.name: Wise Counsellor
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old returning after 92 days (46 since a fall); form figures of 678 on Good suggest he has yet to find his level, and the hold-up style mapped to midfield due to congestion is a secondary concern — the return from a hurdles fall is the primary question mark for Caoilin Quinn.|

races.paceDynamic: Phantom Gold is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just one horse willing to lead from the front in a 12-runner field, she is likely to set a controlled, uncontested gallop throughout the 2m2½f trip on Good ground. The bulk of the field — Wise Counsellor, Makinbecon, Warfleet, Man Oh Man and Saucats — are genuine hold-up types who have been pushed forward on the map simply because they cannot all settle at the rear in this configuration; in reality, several will be competing for midfield berths rather than launching late runs from the back. Chartwell Jock and Privilege offer the most credible prominent coverage behind Phantom Gold, while Katana and Marhaba The Champ represent the truest closing profiles in the race. With a single, unharrassed pace-setter likely to bowl along at a measured gallop, this race shape strongly favours horses that can travel prominently or just off the pace and attack two out, rather than genuine late closers who will need a stronger tempo to get home.

scenarios.body: If Phantom Gold bowls along uncontested and sets a sustainable rhythm that blunts the hold-up horses' finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: C

scenarios.body: If the pace collapses or Phantom Gold burns out early, creating a genuinely strong tempo that drags the hold-up horses into contention off the home turn.

scenarios.label: D

scenarios.body: If the race fragments early — fallers, dramatic checks, or Phantom Gold refusing to go on — producing a muddling pace and a wide-open scramble.

watchPoints.text: Privilege has not run for 334 days and fell last time out — watch for any sign of hesitancy at the early hurdles from this returning chaser, as a mistake or refusal could bring down the horses immediately behind her.

With five genuine hold-up types (Makinbecon, Warfleet, Man Oh Man, Saucats, Wise Counsellor) all jostling for midfield rather than their natural rear positions, watch for significant crowding and checking in the first half-mile as they fail to get organised.

Phantom Gold's price and position as sole front-runner make I J Power's early tactics crucial — if he elects not to lead and Phantom Gold drops in, the race could temporarily have no genuine pacemaker and trigger a slow-motion opening that scrambles the whole field's plans.

Crab Road's tendency to fade in the finish makes him a danger to others rather than a winning contender — watch for him weakening sharply on the long run to the last and causing interference to closers attempting to pick up.|

Chartwell Jock is the one horse with the profile and tactical position to exploit a controlled pace — watch whether Sam Bowen sends him into second or third early, which would set up the most likely alternative winner to the leader.|

races.name: St. Austell Brewery Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Demoiselle Kap
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner who will set the pace from the off; Good ground suits (6/15 placed including a win) and the tongue tie is retained, but racing at the top of the weights (168lbs) and a slight style-fit note (STYLE_FIT=0.93) means her chance is real but not unassailable if Limerick Leader tracks relentlessly.

runners_data.name: Walkin Out
runners_data.note: David Pipe's stayer has an excellent record at this distance and going (7/11 placed, 1W) and Sam Bowen takes over from a 45-day break, making the fitness angle the key question; has the profile of a horse who could finish strongly if the pace is honest enough to stretch the field.

runners_data.name: Limerick Leader
runners_data.note: Remarkably consistent horse who has finished second in four of his last five starts and won the other — all on Good ground at around this trip; Nick Scholfield's yard is 1/7 in the 14-day window and James Bowen is a strong booking; blinkers retained and he looks the most naturally suited to the anticipated race shape.

runners_data.name: Jack's A Legend
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old hold-up performer ridden by conditional Miss Imogen Mathias; went 7th last time out at 21f Good and his recent form figures suggest declining, though he has placed at this trip and going before; tongue tie retained but the age and OR of 94 create doubt.

runners_data.name: Vengeance
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by nature whose true style means this race shape — built around a single front-runner and a modest pace — offers little opportunity to produce his best from the rear; has placed four times on Good ground in recent starts but has yet to win on it, and the style redistribution and STYLE_FIT tag (0.90) both apply here.

runners_data.name: Danny's Friend
runners_data.note: Strong trainer form (Christian Williams 2/13 in 14 days) and Jack Tudor is a top conditional booking, giving this 7-year-old a positive angle; won over Good ground at 16f but is a true closer by inclination, placed here in midfield on the map because of a crowded hold-up division — the trip step-up to 2m5f is also unproven territory.

runners_data.name: School For Scandal
runners_data.note: Veteran of 11 years with a "P" (pulled up) on his last run and question marks over his two longest-trip starts in the form history; three placed efforts at 23f+ on varied going show he stays, but the inconsistency and Callum Pritchard's booking from a 45-day break makes him speculative at best.

races.paceDynamic: Demoiselle Kap is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in this seven-runner field, she will set a controlled, sustainable pace from the outset over 2m5f on Good ground at Newton Abbot. Limerick Leader will press from a prominent position and may provide some company through the early stages, but neither horse is likely to force a truly searching gallop, leaving the pace honest rather than extreme. The redistributed hold-up types — Vengeance and Danny's Friend — are genuine closers by nature but are mapped to midfield because the field contains more rear-runners than the map can accommodate, meaning Walkin Out and Jack's A Legend may also be competing for similar ground further back. A controlled, single-paced gallop over this trip on Good turf strongly favours prominent racers who can travel smoothly in the slipstream of a modest pace and produce their effort from the home turn — Demoiselle Kap's ability to dictate and Limerick Leader's relentless placed form at this sort of mark make the prominent/tracking profile the chief beneficiary.

scenarios.body: If Demoiselle Kap dictates an unchallenged, even gallop and Limerick Leader tracks throughout before a two-horse battle develops from the last.

scenarios.label: D

watchPoints.text: Limerick Leader — if James Bowen positions him immediately behind Demoiselle Kap through the early stages, his relentless placed record and Good-ground form make him the most dangerous horse to Demoiselle Kap's lead at the final fence.

Walkin Out — David Pipe runners returning from 45-day breaks (this one has a 30-day prep race on record) can arrive fit; if Sam Bowen slots him comfortably into mid-division early, his stamina profile at 2m5f Good is the most potent late threat.

Demoiselle Kap's weight — carrying 168lbs as the front-runner over 2m5f on Good ground is a notable burden; if she begins to labour at the third-last, the race will open up quickly for those tracking her.

Vengeance and Danny's Friend — both true hold-up horses mapped to midfield due to redistribution; watch whether C O'Farrell or Jack Tudor attempt to push forward early, as any unexpected change in position could alter the pace picture materially.

School For Scandal's jumping — the "P" last time and two previous "?" results at longer trips suggest his jumping can become ragged; Callum Pritchard should be monitored at the open ditches as any errors will compromise his chance from a prominent position.

races.name: Murray Group Gallop Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Belgarum
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Joe Tizzard (3/11 last 14 days) who has won twice and placed six times in similar going; top-weight at 168lbs over 3m2½f is a stamina question but recent form of 1-2 suggests he remains in form, and unchallenged control of the pace is his best weapon.

runners_data.name: Striking A Pose
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up horse with two wins and five places in similar good-ground form figures; Brendan Powell fits a stayer who needs a strong gallop to reel in rivals, and a 28-day absence for the same trainer barn as Belgarum is worth monitoring for stable intentions.

runners_data.name: Balkardy
runners_data.note: Older hold-up type (9yo) in modest recent form (5-6-P-U-7) with Eleanor Williams aboard and the trainer's yard showing zero wins from three in the last fortnight; the going poses no issue but the form string offers limited confidence, and similar-going figures of 0W0P in 15 runs are a concern.

runners_data.name: Cinnodin
runners_data.note: Sharp six-year-old in excellent recent form (3-2-5-1-2) for Jamie Snowden whose yard is firing (6/13 last 14 days); a natural hold-up horse who wears a hood and will likely push forward given the field dynamics, and that adaptability — combined with strong good-ground credentials — makes the redistribution to a prominent role potentially advantageous rather than costly.

runners_data.name: Jafimgoso
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton and Dan Skelton (11/23 last 14 days) is a potent combination on a seven-year-old who has won twice on good ground over similar trips; a true rear-runner by inclination who will need to race against his instincts in this shape, though the Skelton team are expert at adjusting tactics and two of his last four runs ended in victory.

runners_data.name: I Am Spider Man
runners_data.note: James Bowen partners this nine-year-old who has placed repeatedly over 3m-plus on good ground (3-2-2 in last five comparable runs) for Barry Murphy; a consistent hold-up performer over this sort of trip, though the trainer's yard is quiet (0/5 last 14 days) and he will need a stronger gallop than Belgarum alone may generate.

runners_data.name: Jager Time
runners_data.note: Fern O'Brien rides her trainer father's seven-year-old who has a fine recent record (2-2-1-4-3) over staying trips on good ground; a hold-up type who races in a pattern suggesting he needs a genuinely run race to peel off the back, and his redistribution to midfield reflects the field's overcrowding rather than a change of gear.

runners_data.name: Final Entry
runners_data.note: Youngest runner in the field at five, lightly weighted at 156lbs, and trained by David Pipe (0/7 last 14 days) with Jack Tudor up; recent form shows a third last time out over this exact trip on good ground, though the experience gap against older handicappers is real and the headgear combination of tongue strap and visor suggests the yard is working to find his best.

races.paceDynamic: Belgarum is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 3m2½f handicap hurdle and, with no rival likely to press him for the lead, he should dictate at a measured, sustainable gallop on good ground at Newton Abbot. The field is stacked with hold-up horses — Cinnodin, Jafimgoso, I Am Spider Man, Jager Time, and Final Entry are all genuine come-from-behind types, meaning the race will almost certainly string out behind Belgarum with a compressed chase pack hunting him down from two out. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; of those redistributed to midfield, Jafimgoso and Cinnodin — both carrying strong recent form and handled by shrewd handlers — are most likely to secure a forward position ahead of their natural role. With one horse dictating an honest but uncontested pace over a stamina-testing trip, this race shape strongly favours horses that can travel prominently or just off the pace and sustain their effort through the final climb, rather than pure closers who will face too much ground to make up late.

scenarios.title: Belgarum Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Belgarum is allowed to bowl along in front at his own tempo with no rival prepared to close him down early.
scenarios.body: If Belgarum is allowed to bowl along in front at his own tempo with no rival prepared to close him down early.

scenarios.title: Pace Increases Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If the chasing pack collectively refuses to be left and a cluster of rivals move up to challenge Belgarum turning for home, raising the overall tempo.
scenarios.body: If the chasing pack collectively refuses to be left and a cluster of rivals move up to challenge Belgarum turning for home, raising the overall tempo.

scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through

scenarios.body: If Belgarum fades in the final mile after front-running for too long, gifting genuine stayers the chance to wear him down.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If a high rate of jumping errors or fallers disrupts the field mid-race, altering natural positioning and creating an unpredictable finish.
scenarios.body: If a high rate of jumping errors or fallers disrupts the field mid-race, altering natural positioning and creating an unpredictable finish.

watchPoints.text: Belgarum — if he is allowed to stride clear by two or three lengths through the back straight unchallenged, the race is effectively run to his strengths and hold-up horses face a near-impossible task on this stiff 3m2½f trip.

Cinnodin and Jafimgoso — both natural hold-up types facing the prospect of racing outside their comfort zone in a prominent role; if either becomes unsettled by an unnatural position in the early stages, their finishing run could be compromised.
Balkardy — the U (unseated) in recent form on good ground and a record of 0W0P in 15 similar-going runs is a live jumping-safety concern in a race of this distance and trip.

Striking A Pose and Belgarum share the same trainer (Joe Tizzard, 3/11 last 14 days) — monitor market moves for any sign of stable preference, as both are prominent in the pace map at the top of the weights.

Final Entry — at only five years old tackling 3m2½f in a competitive handicap, watch for signs of greenness or jumping hesitancy in the early stages; if he travels fluently, his light weight and youth could make him a durable stayer in the straight.

races.name: Thatchers Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Jetty May
runners_data.note: P F Nicholls runner with a strong Good-ground profile (6/7 outings on similar going, one win, one place); hold-up style suits a race where the hold-up bunch is large but she has shown the class to work through traffic at 3m-plus, and 31 days off is a manageable break; tongue-strap worn.

runners_data.name: Edgewell
runners_data.note: Excellent Good-ground record (10/15 outings, 2 wins, 6 places) is the standout angle here; Nick Scholfield's yard in decent recent form at 1/8 over 14 days, and 13 days since last run means this horse is race-fit; a natural hold-up type who needs to find a clear passage but has the experience over 25-26f trips to do so.

runners_data.name: Hatos
runners_data.note: Tizzard yard fielding at 3/8 recent runners; this horse's natural style is hold-up and while Good ground is within range, all five recent outings have been 20f or shorter — the step up to 3m2f is the key query, and an unresolved "?" in the distance column of his Good-ground history adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Illogical Logic
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner and the pace anchor for the whole field; Christian Williams yard modest at 1/15 over 14 days and 65 days off is a slight flag, but his recent Good-ground record (9/15 runs) and front-running identity mean he will set the race's tempo regardless — the STYLE_FIT tag notes he is racing in his natural role here, not out of it.

runners_data.name: Honey I'm Good
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse whose natural rear-of-field position is congested in this field, meaning she is likely to settle midfield rather than where she is most comfortable; Mrs C Williams yard active at 2/13, but 71 days since last run and a "?" in her most recent going entry adds uncertainty, and the STYLE_FIT discount is genuine given the crowded hold-up group.

runners_data.name: Bucks Dream
runners_data.note: 106 days off (last run a pulled-up effort) is a significant concern for a 10-year-old; naturally a hold-up horse whose chances are squeezed by the redistribution — the field's structure means clean late ground will be hard to find — and a Good-ground record of 0W/4P from 6 outings gives limited confidence in an upswing here.

runners_data.name: Unspeakable
runners_data.note: Carries top-weight credentials for a prominent racer and Jack Tudor is a high-quality pilot; Good-ground record of 10/15 with 2 wins and 5 places is competitive, and 30 days since last run is fresh enough; needs to justify prominent position by pressing Illogical Logic rather than sitting passive.

runners_data.name: Testflight
runners_data.note: Tabitha Worsley takes the ride for Mrs S Gardner's yard (0/5 over 14 days, a cold stat); consistent place record on Good (10/15, 1W, 7P) but no wins in six recent starts suggests a horse who hits the frame without quite getting over the line — prominent style could work here if tempo allows.

runners_data.name: Benny Baloo
runners_data.note: 123 days off is the longest layoff in the field for a 9-year-old, and his Good-ground form is thin (3/14, 0W, 1P); genuinely a hold-up type forced into a midfield berth by the race's shape, and the STYLE_FIT tag combined with the extended absence makes it hard to construct a convincing winning scenario without a major bounce-back.

races.paceDynamic: Illogical Logic is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 3m2f handicap chase and, with no other horse naturally inclined to lead, should secure an uncontested, low-pressure gallop from the outset. Honey I'm Good, Bucks Dream, and Benny Baloo are genuine hold-up horses who have been redistributed toward midfield on the map — in practice, the rear of the field will be crowded with closers jostling for similar ground, meaning none of them will enjoy a clean, unimpeded passage. Unspeakable and Testflight add a secondary prominent presence and may push into the slipstream of Illogical Logic, creating a small leading group but unlikely to fundamentally alter the tempo given the relaxed pace Illogical Logic typically sets. This race shape — a lone leader, moderate gallop, and a compressed hold-up bunch hunting the same late ground — strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or close from a genuine midfield berth without needing the back of the pack all to themselves; patient prominent racers and adaptable mid-division types with good course and going form are best placed here.

scenarios.title: Prominent Upsets Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Unspeakable or Testflight tracks Illogical Logic closely and delivers a challenge from the second-last fence, catching the front-runner flat-footed.
scenarios.body: If Unspeakable or Testflight tracks Illogical Logic closely and delivers a challenge from the second-last fence, catching the front-runner flat-footed.

watchPoints.text: Illogical Logic jumps from the front alone — if he makes a jumping error at any of the early fences without a rival to steady the pace, the tempo collapse could reshuffle the entire race shape far earlier than expected.

Honey I'm Good, Bucks Dream, and Benny Baloo will all be hunting the same late ground from the rear; watch for significant crowding and interference on the home turn as none of them can get their natural position, potentially costing the most talented of the three a clean run.

Edgewell's 13-day turnaround is tight for a hold-up chaser over 3m2f — if Harry Reed settles him too far back early and the pace is steady, he may never get into the contest before the field stretches out at the final fence.

Testflight's record of seven places from ten Good-ground runs without a win in recent starts is worth flagging — in a race where the pace is controlled and no one is forced wide, the horse who can peel out neatly at the second-last has a clear profile advantage that Testflight has repeatedly come close to fulfilling.

Bucks Dream's last run being a pulled-up effort followed by a 106-day break is the longest recovery window in this field; monitor the market for any late support that might signal stable confidence in a revival, otherwise treat the form blank as a meaningful negative.
